title: Copilot Studio: cost controls in the Microsoft 365 admin center
summary: The briefing accurately describes the opt-in spending policies and their replacement of covered Power Platform allocations and billing plans. The control paths, commands and billing claims are supported; Microsoft's conflicting descriptions of License Administrator permissions merit a small clarification.

claims.claim: The control is admin-opt-in, leaving the existing Power Platform configuration in effect until a resource-based policy is created.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The consumption licensing model reflects governed Copilot Credit usage funded by pay-as-you-go, P3 or prepaid capacity packs.
claims.quote: Depending on the service, organizations can use fixed licensing, the Copilot Credit Pre-purchase Plan (P3), pay-as-you-go billing, prepaid capacity packs, or supported combinations of these billing methods.

claims.claim: No separate licence or charge for the cost controls is stated as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio cost management controls separate license price resource based spending policies. Read the feature, setup and usage-based billing overview pages; none states a separate control licence or charge.

claims.claim: The feature page's Before you begin section lists Microsoft 365 roles, not a licence or price prerequisite for the control.
claims.quote: Before creating a resource-based spending policy for Copilot Studio agents, ensure that you have the necessary roles in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The resource-policy creation path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy > Resources > Specific environments.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Cost Management. ... Select Configuration, and then select Add spending policy. ... select Resources as its scope. ... Specific environments: Choose Specific environments when you want to move and manage a limited set of environments first.

claims.claim: No Graph call for resource-based environment or agent spending policies is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio resource based spending policy Microsoft Graph API environment agent policy. Read Cost Management API overview and spendingPolicy resource reference; the documented derived policy types cover all users or selected groups, not resources.

claims.claim: Capacity allocation is reached at Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: select Licensing. ... under Products, select Copilot Studio. ... Select the Summary tab. ... Under the Copilot Studio heading, select Manage Copilot Credits or Manage sessions.

claims.claim: pac licensing update-allocations-by-environment --environment-id <environment-id> --currency-allocations <JSON array> updates environment allocations and enforcement rules.
claims.quote: Update currency allocations and enforcement rules for an environment. ... --currency-allocations ... including enforcement rules such as TenantPool ... Provide the value as a JSON array. ... --environment-id ... The environment ID.

claims.claim: Individual agent monthly limits can be set from Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Manage Agents.
claims.quote: select Licensing. ... under Products, select Copilot Studio. ... On the Summary tab, select Manage Agents. ... You can set a monthly limit for any agent directly from this page.

claims.claim: These references do not document a Copilot Studio-specific API for its monthly per-agent limit.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio monthly per agent consumption limit API pac licensing threshold. Read capacity management and pac licensing, including upsert-resource-threshold; the latter documents generic environment-resource thresholds without identifying this Copilot Studio setting.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go billing plan creation starts at Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Pay-as-you-go plans > New billing plan > Azure subscription.
claims.quote: select Licensing. ... select Pay-as-you-go plans. ... Select New billing plan. ... Select Azure subscription.

claims.claim: pac licensing create-billing-policy creates the billing policy used by the following environment-linking command.
claims.quote: pac licensing create-billing-policy ... (Preview) Creates the billing policy at tenant level.

claims.claim: pac licensing add-billing-policy-environment --billing-policy-id <id> --environment-ids <JSON array> links environments to a billing policy.
claims.quote: Link billing policy ID with environments. ... --billing-policy-id ... The billing policy ID. ... --environment-ids ... Provide the value as a JSON array.

claims.claim: The listed pac licensing commands are marked Preview.
claims.quote: (Preview) Manage licensing, entitlements, capacity, billing policies, and allocations.

claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio cost management rollout resource. Read the supplied roadmap and feature, setup and overview pages; these describe the experience but give no all-tenant completion date or tenant-specific availability.

claims.quote: Searched: agent registry cost Copilot Studio; Copilot Studio agent registry cost data metadata cost November 2026. Read Agent registry integration for Copilot Studio, including Visible metadata and Agent details page; neither lists a cost field.

claims.claim: The same Microsoft 365 Cost Management dashboard supports other usage-based Copilot services and read-only finance or licensing stakeholders.
claims.quote: This separation enables finance, operations, licensing, and governance stakeholders to review consumption information with read-only access.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance

claims.quote: Review consumption by spending policy, user, group, agent, service, and funding source.

claims.claim: Existing Power Platform roles do not themselves confer Microsoft 365 spending-policy roles.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not describe the precise agent behavior when a resource-based policy limit is reached.

Read the feature and manage-credits pages; resource policy limits and no identity fallback are stated, but precise agent behavior is not.

claims.claim: Power Platform documents a configurable per-agent hard stop that turns the agent off at its limit.
claims.quote: After you set limits, you can configure two key guardrails: ... Hard stop: The agent is automatically turned off once it hits the defined limit.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio Microsoft 365 cost management resource spending policy limit reached agent stops rollout availability license cost controls. Read feature policy hierarchy and capacity-management agent limits; precedence is explicit, but continued PPAC hard-stop enforcement is not.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 spending-policy controls take precedence over Power Platform controls for covered usage.
claims.quote: If a spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center covers the environment or agent, its controls take precedence over the Power Platform admin center controls for that usage.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Scope
claims.claim: Resource-based policies do not apply to AI Builder features or the credits those features consume.
claims.quote: Resource-based policies created in the Microsoft 365 admin center don't apply to AI Builder features or the credits they consume.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: AI Builder powers prompts used as tools, in topics and as agent-flow nodes.

claims.where: Scope: Out of scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout

claims.quote: Don't move resources, agents, workflows or environments that use AI Builder to these policies.

claims.claim: A resource-based policy takes precedence over an identity-based policy.
claims.quote: Resource-based policy before identity-based policy. Within the Microsoft 365 admin center, a policy for the agent or its environment takes precedence over a policy for the person using the agent.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Where resource-based policies overlap, the policy with the higher applicable per-agent limit applies.
claims.quote: If you have a resource-based All-environments policy and a Specific resource HR agent policy, the policy with the higher per-agent limit applies.

claims.claim: Limits from overlapping policies are not added together.
claims.quote: Spending limits from overlapping policies aren't combined.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Power Platform's Manage capacity experience indicates when a Microsoft 365 policy manages an environment's Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: the Manage capacity experience indicates when Copilot Credits for an environment are managed by a Microsoft 365 admin center resource-based spending policy

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The Manage agent experience displays a message when a policy covers the agent.
claims.quote: The Manage agent experience also displays a message when an agent is covered by a policy.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The governed usage is metered in Copilot Credits, supporting the variable cost rating.
claims.quote: Microsoft's usage-based billing model charges customers based on actual usage, measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The subscription selected in the billing method is billed for Copilot Credit usage.
claims.quote: Copilot credits are billed to the subscription that you select in the billing method.

claims.claim: When credits for the selected subscription run out, usage continues on pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: When credits run out for that subscription, usage automatically continues on a pay-as-you-go basis.

claims.claim: P3 is layered on top of pay-as-you-go, rather than being a separate billing option.
claims.quote: Copilot Credit Pre-Purchase Plan (P3) and pay-as-you-go aren't separate billing options. P3 is layered on top of pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: P3 can be purchased from Cost Management > Configuration or the Azure portal.
claims.quote: by selecting Buy Pre-purchase Credits on the Cost Management > Configuration page. You can also complete this step through the Azure portal.

claims.claim: When both prepaid capacity packs and a P3 subscription are selected, the documented order is capacity packs, P3, then pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: If you select both Prepaid Capacity packs and an Azure subscription with Copilot Credit Pre-purchase plan (P3), billing is applied in the following order ... Prepaid Capacity packs ... Copilot Credit Pre-purchase plan (P3) ... Pay-as-you-go billing

claims.claim: Prepaid capacity pack credits can support services managed in either admin center.
claims.quote: Prepaid Capacity pack credits can support services managed in either admin center.

claims.claim: Power Platform environment allocations reduce credits available to other services in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Credits allocated to environments in the Power Platform admin center reduce the credits available for other services in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Apps and workflows cannot be selected individually and instead need environment coverage.
claims.quote: Apps and workflows don't currently appear in the agent selector, so you can't select an individual app or workflow. To cover them, create a policy for the environment where they're deployed.

claims.claim: The feature page recommends AI Administrator for Power Platform or Dynamics 365 Administrators managing spending policies.
claims.quote: Power Platform Administrator or Dynamics 365 Administrator | AI Administrator | Manage spending policies.

claims.claim: The feature page recommends AI Reader for Environment Administrators who need to view consumption.
claims.quote: Environment Administrator | AI Reader | View consumption when needed.

claims.claim: The setup page lists Global administrator or Billing administrator for initial policy creation, while the feature page recommends AI Administrator for policy management.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center with one of the following administrator roles: ... Global administrator ... Billing administrator

claims.claim: An identity-based policy cannot be converted into a resource-based policy; a new resource-based policy must be created.
claims.quote: You can't convert an existing identity-based policy into a resource-based policy. To manage a resource or environment when you have only an identity-based policy, create a new resource-based policy.

claims.claim: The documented Graph Cost Management policy scopes are all users and selected groups.
claims.quote: Scope a policy to every user in the tenant (allUsersSpendingPolicy) or to selected groups (selectedGroupsSpendingPolicy).

claims.claim: pac licensing documents generic environment-resource threshold automation.
claims.quote: pac licensing upsert-resource-threshold ... (Preview) Create or update the resource threshold for an environment resource.

claims.claim: Environment admin, Power Platform admin, Global admin and Dynamics 365 admin can create billing policies.
claims.quote: Environment admin | Yes ... Power Platform admin | Yes ... Global admin | Yes ... Dynamics 365 admin | Yes

claims.claim: Environment admins can edit only billing policies they created.
claims.quote: Environment admin ... Yes, for billing policies the admin created.

claims.claim: The Graph Cost Management beta APIs are subject to change and not supported in production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Billing setup requires Azure resource-creation and resource-provider-registration permissions, or help from a user with those permissions.
claims.quote: You need to have permissions to create new resources and register resource providers in the subscription—or have the ability to work with another user who has these permissions.

claims.claim: Power Platform per-agent limits provide notifications as usage approaches the defined limit.
claims.quote: Notifications: Admins, both at the environment and tenant level, receive alerts when an agent's usage approaches the defined limit.

claims.claim: Cost Management supports reviewing consumption by environment and agent.
claims.quote: You can view consumption by environment and agent.

claims.claim: An environment's overage setting can allow continued consumption from available tenant capacity.
claims.quote: Select Draw from the available capacity in my tenant to let the environment use unallocated prepaid capacity from the tenant pool.

claims.claim: An environment's overage setting can allow continued usage through its pay-as-you-go billing plan.
claims.quote: Select Bill to my pay-as-you-go billing plan to let the environment continue usage through the selected billing plan.

claims.claim: Environment admins can link only billing policies they created to environments they administer.
claims.quote: Environment admin ... Yes, for billing policies the admin created and for environments in which they're admins.

claims.claim: Power Platform per-agent limits are not applied instantly.
claims.quote: Limits aren't applied instantly. An agent can continue to respond for some time after it reaches its limit, so set limits and notification thresholds with some margin.
